gaps.sentence: We ___ the risk of flooding very seriously.
gaps.explanation: 'Take something seriously' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: You should ___ track of your spending.
gaps.explanation: keep track of something means to stay informed about it.

gaps.sentence: The ___ traffic added an hour to our journey.
gaps.explanation: heavy traffic means a lot of vehicles on the road; 'thick traffic' is not standard.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: The judge ___ the verdict after four hours of deliberation.
gaps.explanation: 'Deliver a verdict/judgement' is the legal collocation.

gaps.sentence: The boy knew it was wrong to ___ lies.
gaps.explanation: tell a lie / tell lies is the fixed collocation; a base verb is needed after 'to'.

gaps.sentence: We stayed indoors because of the ___ rain.
gaps.explanation: heavy rain is the standard collocation; 'strong rain' is not used.

gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.
